newsitem.title: UK: Brent paper slips, physical assessed weaker.
newsitem.headline: Brent paper slips, physical assessed weaker.

text.p: North Sea Brent fell on the paper market on Thursday with intermonth spreads and CFDs coming off too. Physical barrels were notionally weaker, sapped by a lack of demand, traders said. "There's no buying interest and there's no selling interest," one trader said of the physical market.
On cash, July Brent dropped sharply, trading 27 cents down at $18.45 a barrel by 1248 GMT.
No outrights were heard traded after August Brent partials sold at $18.78, $18.80, $18.83 and $18.84 on the U.S. aftermarket.

Brent intermonth spreads and Contracts for Difference were not heard traded but both came off. Jun/Jul was five cents softer talked -35/-28 cents and Jul/Aug shed four cents to talk -23/-21 cents. Contracts for Differences for next week (Jun 9-13) slipped three cents, offered at July Brent -45 cents, while the following week was offered four cents down at July -37 cents. One Brent cargo was turning wet on Thursday. The cargo is due to load June 20-22.
Traders said physical Brent continues to be pressured from ample June supply.
A closed arbitrage to the U.S.made matters worse.
"There a total lack of action, there's supply but demand is very low...The bears are winning for the moment," one trader said. "We have to wait and see if the United States comes in."

Other traders said that refiners were relaxed with several unsold June cargoes around. "There still seems to be a few Brent cargoes to sell. I have a (June) 16-18 cargo but I am not really showing it out on the market at the moment, there are people who have earlier cargoes, let's see what they do first," one seller said.

"The market seems to be pretty quiet," he said adding that the arbitrage to the United States "does not work at the moment." Some traders said other North Sea grade differentials were assessed weaker on Thursday.

Two sellers were heard offering Statfjord at Wednesday's level of Dated Brent +25 cents, which was three cents below a trade a day earlier. Late third decade Forties was also heard offered at similar numbers to Statfjord.

"There are still a few cargoes lying around but it is into diabolically bad, but there are some cargoes, there's Ekofisk, a bit of Oseberg and Staffjord," one trader said. Other traders said Ekofisk was assessed around Dated Brent +18 cents and that Oseberg, valued previously in the Dated Brent plus mid to high teens, could be picked up close to Dated evens. In the Mediterranean, Russian Urals seems to steady to a shade stronger after a few cargoes found homes in the last two days, some traders said. One Italian refiner said he bought a large cargo of Urals late on Wednesday but said the deal was private and confidential. The deal meant that only one or two large June cargoes of the sour crude were still unsold. Other traders said that there was little action on the market early on Thursday, adding buyers may hold off for a day or two as several cargoes have been snatched up. They said Urals was assessed in the Dated Brent -$1.40/-$1.30 region for buyers and sellers respectively.
